# Supplied discovery

This is a constructed planning fixture. Source, tests and data are present; the baseline suite passed. Only existing behavior was tested. No new feature, atomicity or search acceptance is implied. No earlier decision experiment is supplied.

# Architecture

## Stack

Python standard library; sqlite3; installed src/adapter.py VERSION 2.3.

## Structure

Preserve src/adapter.py and tests/test_baseline.py. Proposed src/importer.py owns validation/staging/publication, src/__main__.py owns argparse/JSON CLI, tests/test_import.py owns regressions. Product feature unimplemented during planning. Local Python resolves the existing src package from worktree root; src.__main__ is currently absent. New importer imports .adapter; CLI imports .importer. Export import_batch(db_path, rows) only for CLI/tests, keep stage/publication helpers private. New tests/import_support.py contains disposable fixtures and controlled child lifecycle; tests/test_import_support.py checks those facilities independently before tests/test_import.py consumes them. No namespace collision exists in the supplied tree. No remote runtime.

Existing/destination schema stays inventory(sku TEXT PRIMARY KEY, quantity INTEGER), owned by installed adapter; SKU key, quantity value, no relationships or new schema/version migration. Wrapper validates required types, does not alter adapter DDL. Existing unrelated tables/triggers/rows must survive snapshot. Candidate is never authoritative; live path is authority. Owner-local disk permissions must be preserved on replacement. Stage lifetime is one attempt; abrupt-death orphan inert until owner cleanup. No sensitive fields, quota or workload SLA supplied; no invented store. Reject symlink and multiply linked live paths using lexical lstat before resolve; preserve existing POSIX mode. Fail-closed path/journal behavior is required retained implementation coverage; no hostile directory mutation/concurrent writer assumed.

## Conventions

Small explicit functions, unittest, disposable fixtures. Match adapter's path-oriented interface and baseline's sqlite3 independent observation. Bounded subprocess timeouts and structured argv.

## Interfaces and boundaries

Installed apply(db_path,rows) retains row application; never pass visible live path during batch mutation. It commits a prefix even when later row fails and an outer connection rolls back (owned scratch/characterize.log).

Proposed CLI: python3 -B -m src import-json --db PATH --file JSON_PATH. Validate complete input before effects; create unique candidate in destination directory; consistently snapshot existing database using sqlite3 backup, preserving rows and schema; apply installed adapter to candidate; close/check/flush; publish once via os.replace. Never create live DB before success when absent. Caught failures remove only owned stage; abrupt-death leftovers inert, never auto-promoted. Local probe supports this route for clean DELETE-journal regular paths on the supplied runtime. Reject WAL/non-DELETE mode, any live -wal/-shm/-journal sidecar, invalid DB or unresolved alias before live effects; never switch live mode to force support. WAL main-file replacement with active sidecars was observed to produce a malformed read. Missing DB initializes privately and publishes only on success. Stage cleanup begins immediately after creation and spans snapshot errors as well as adapter/publication errors; a cleanup error never withdraws committed visibility.

Publication is linearization point. Before it, invalid record, adapter error or interruption preserves old visible state. At/after it, reopened readers see complete committed batch. Termination after replace but before success output cannot guarantee old state without withdrawing already visible committed data. Treat as committed with acknowledgement unknown and allow idempotent retry. This is an explicit planning interpretation/limitation of literal "any interrupted import", not proof of that stronger promise. Test both sides; never accept prefix. Process-kill evidence does not establish host power-loss guarantees.

## Real-boundary checks

Local Python subprocess, reopened SQLite and filesystem are actual consumer boundary. W1 owns checked test helpers; W2 owns TC_1..TC_8, due implement/test then system-test/product-acceptance. No concurrent writer. CLI actor can write only disposable test targets.

Planned TC_1 procedure: seed old=2,keep=7; write [{"sku":"old","quantity":11},{"sku":"new","quantity":3}] to scratch JSON; invoke actual CLI; check exit 0 and success; independently reopen sorted inventory and expect keep=7,new=3,old=11; repeat exact command and expect identical table. R-1 permits updates by SKU, insertion and preservation. Oracle independently computed: overwrite old, insert new, leave keep. No product execution claimed.

TC_2: old=11,bad=-1,tail=3 input expects original keep=7,old=2 after error. TC_3: bad=5 with independently installed trigger rejecting bad, same original expected after adapter error; snapshot must preserve trigger. TC_4/5: fresh base, readiness after prefix and prereplace, kill/reap child, reopen old table, fresh process retry valid batch yields success, replay identical. TC_6: checkpoint after replace then kill yields complete committed success. Each is planned; durable process assertions remain due.

Remote services, cache, auth, async event delivery and operator log contracts are absent from request/application. No remote endpoint or credential authorized; external compatibility unverified. Browser/native UI not applicable to CLI-only surface. No local result is remote evidence.

## Decisions

AD-1: Preserve standard-library stack and baseline.
AD-2: Keep installed adapter, isolate partial commits with candidate publication rather than rewrite row application. Evidence: owned scratch/characterize.py and characterize.log.
AD-3: Consistent sqlite3.backup, installed adapter on private same-directory candidate, close/check/fsync, one os.replace commit point. Selected after disposable process-kill/retry/error probes; outer live transaction rejected. Support clean DELETE journal only; reject WAL/live sidecars and aliases before effects. Naive active-WAL replacement observed malformed read. Evidence: owned planning experiment decision.md and raw logs (exact locators in accepted plan result). Revalidate filesystem/runtime or adapter changes. Postcommit acknowledgement and power-loss limitations remain explicit.

AD-4: Namespace responsibility split above; existing src.adapter stays unchanged; local module CLI adds no external runtime. Rationale: path-based adapter reuse and one isolated publication responsibility; alternative monolithic adapter edit would change existing client contract.
AD-5: Storage shape unchanged; preserve schema/rows/POSIX mode, private initial file, no migration. Candidate never authoritative until single replacement; owned stale stages inert and never auto-promoted. Fail closed on unsupported journal/path state per AD-3; do not mutate live database during preflight or snapshot. Alternative in-place migration unnecessary. Durable behavior still due W2 TC_3..7.
AD-6: Interaction remains synchronous local CLI -> validation -> candidate adapter -> single publication -> success output. No acceptance acknowledgement or background processing before commit; failures report stderr/nonzero without false success. No UI/async channels/cache/connection quota; static text CLI feedback. Power-loss durability and success-output delivery are separate from atomic visibility and remain disclosed limits.

## Superseded

Naive outer transaction around adapter.apply: different connection plus row commits leave visible prefix on failure.

# Environment

## Targets and runtimes

Local Python 3.9.6, sqlite3 3.54.0 on macOS; standard library only. Tests target disposable databases in owned scratch. No concurrent writers; readers reopen paths between commands. data/seed.json is read-only input, never a database target. Probe: RUN/scratch/characterize.py and characterize.log (RUN is the recorded run evidence root).
